runtime: Repository-pinned Bun 1.4.2, disposable PostgreSQL, synthetic connectors

findings.problem: Restart recovery labeled unreadable completed connector responses as failed/not delivered even though live delivery labeled them unknown.
findings.before: Completed opaque-text/MCP error records settled failed.
findings.fix: Recovery preserves uncertainty, forbids replay and creates no settled-success/failure wake.

findings.problem: Empty objects and arrays were accepted as successful connector replies.
findings.before: A completed empty/array reply settled sent.
findings.fix: Reject empty objects and arrays as unreadable; both immediate automatic results and recovered cards stay unknown.

findings.problem: Cards stored mutable account namespaces, so renaming an account broke a reviewed draft.
findings.before: Renaming the account left the reviewed send pending with a route error.
findings.fix: New cards bind the verified connection UUID. Legacy cards recover only a unique original account from their exact durable verification calls, with bot/run ownership. No namespace is re-resolved for a legacy send.
checks: Rename without replacement still sends once from original account
A replacement reusing the old namespace cannot take over current or verified legacy email/Slack cards
Missing verification records or a lookalike call-ID prefix refuse sending; the card remains discardable

findings.problem: Recovery trusted a completed call-ID match without checking the bot, run, account or send tool.
findings.before: A completed record belonging to another bot settled the card sent.
findings.fix: Confirm all four identities before treating the saved response as a send; mismatches remain unknown and are never replayed.

reviewChecks: Repeated send/refresh/cancel actions retain one outcome and wake with no transport replay
Canonical route comparisons preserve revision highlighting across a legacy namespace and rename
validation.uniqueCounting: 53 draft integration plus 31 adjacent checks. Three repeat cycles add 18 case executions separately. Earlier broad matrices are historical and are not added to this count.

computerUse.method: Native cua_repl Chrome actions on the actual ExternalDraftCard component, isolated services and synthetic connector; stored connector replies are held until recovery runs.
finalObservations: Visible fixture status confirms account rename and replacement creation completed before any send
Held sends show Sending with Send/Discard disabled
Unreadable and wrong-tool completed records recover as Unconfirmed
Late responses cannot overwrite those terminal outcomes
Third synthetic send succeeds through the original UUID even though a replacement owns the old name
One truthful acknowledgement reports two unconfirmed cards
computerUse.cleanup: Own tabs closed and both temporary UI fixtures removed; disposable records cleared and PostgreSQL stopped.

diagnosticCorrections: The first native harness renamed the account but failed to create its replacement because a local variable shadowed the connection name. A backend assertion caught this; the native name-reuse claim was withdrawn and the corrected fresh three-card test visibly confirmed completion and passed backend route assertions. The first native run is exploratory evidence only.

Canonicalizing new account routes initially prevented highlighting against a legacy namespace baseline. A failing regression prompted normalizing the proven legacy baseline route; exact revised text and added words now pass.

An early filtered integration invocation used the default five-second test timeout and timed out while running six fixtures under load. Final invocations use the existing integration command timeout of thirty seconds; no production timeout was changed.
limits: Finite diagnostic tests cannot establish that every possible issue is absent.
No new live-model or native Grokbot comparison this pass.
No real email/Slack send, APNs delivery, deployment or production treatment change.
Earlier iOS SDK/build and desktop size-budget failures plus environment-specific skips were not revalidated by this server-focused pass.
Legacy cards without sufficient durable verification evidence are refused rather than guessing their original account; they remain discardable.
Recovery validates receipt ownership and reply readability; it does not semantically verify arbitrary connector content or model prose.
No public tool, database migration, approval behavior, signature control or dependency was added.
